title: Good in this world and the next
hookLine: the short du'a from the Qur'an: our Lord, give us good here and good hereafter (2:201)

lines: A MAN LIKE A BABY BIRD.
THE PROPHET GIVES HIM A BETTER ONE.
cards: A man has grown so sick and thin that, in the report's words, he looks like a baby bird. The Prophet ﷺ visits him and asks what he's been praying for. His answer is startling.
Some people, when they finally get the chance to ask for something, ask for too little: just get me through this week. Others turn it into a grand, dramatic bargain. Both are very human.
This man, in a story from Sahih Muslim, did the dramatic kind. And the Prophet gave him a better prayer.

teach.b: The man said: I've been asking Allah, whatever punishment You'd give me in the next life, give it to me now, in this one. He was trying to get it over with.
The Prophet told him he couldn't bear that, and asked why he didn't say instead the du'a from Surah al-Baqarah, verse two hundred one. In Pickthall's translation: Our Lord!
Give unto us in the world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and guard us from the doom of Fire. The report says the man prayed it, and Allah healed him.

In Arabic it begins rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan: our Lord, give us in this world good. The word for good, hasanah, shares its root letters with ihsan, excellence, and husn, beauty. It isn't narrow.
Commentators such as Ibn Kathir read good in this world widely: health, knowledge, a good spouse, honest provision. The verse doesn't choose; it leaves the space open. Notice its shape.
In the verse just before, the Qur'an describes people who only ask, give us in this world, and stop. This du'a asks for both.
Not this life instead of the next, or the next instead of this one.

teach.h: HASANAH — A WIDE WORD FOR GOOD.
BOTH, NOT ONE OR THE OTHER.
teach.b: Anas, who served the Prophet, said in Bukhari that this was the du'a he made most often.
Abu Dawud reports the Prophet saying it while circling the Kaaba, between two of its corners, and pilgrims say it there still.
Some people close their own du'a with it, as a way of asking for everything they forgot to mention.

how: Muslims often recite 2:201, rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan, at the end of their du'a, in the prayer, and while circling the Kaaba between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone.

o: a wide word for good, kin to beauty
a small word for luck, kin to chance
the hope of being healed from illness

games.q: what's inside the du'a of 2:201 — tap the pairs.
p: good, sharing a root with beauty
said it was the Prophet's most frequent du'a

s: the Prophet ﷺ encouraged the sick man's prayer to be punished now
he said the man couldn't bear it and taught him 2:201 instead (Muslim).
the du'a asks for good in both this world and the hereafter
not one instead of the other: good here, good there, and protection from the Fire.
hasanah only means religious good deeds
commentators such as Ibn Kathir read it widely: health, knowledge, a good spouse, honest provision.

games.q: you're so ill you look like a baby bird, and you've been praying to take all your punishment now. the Prophet ﷺ visits. what does he tell you to say?
o: keep praying the same thing, harder
our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter
games.why: he taught him 2:201, and the report says the man prayed it and was healed (Muslim 2688).

practice: If you like, raise your hands, palms up.

If you pray, say the verse once, slowly: rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan, wa fil-akhirati hasanatan, wa qina 'adhaban-nar; or in English: our Lord, give us good in this world, and good in the hereafter, and guard us from the Fire.
If you don't pray, think of one good you want here and one good you'd want to last beyond it, and hold both at once.

wordCard.voice: Hasanah, good: the word at the heart of the short du'a in Surah al-Baqarah, asking for good here, good hereafter, and protection.

orig.note: Arabic: our Lord, give us in this world good, the opening of 2:201.

carryVoice: Your line: good here, good there. Not one or the other: both. Day one hundred thirty-three, done.

sources.q: Our Lord! Give unto us in the world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and guard us from the doom of Fire.
